between: museum-framework.md §4.5, display rules for Relationship Objects: "Alternatives are one interaction away from every bridge. Selecting a bridge shows its rivals at the same visual weight as itself, per §3.10's refusal to let layout settle a question."
and: museum-framework.md §12.3 constraint V-8: "Equal visual weight is a claim, and is only made where the evidence is equal. Two rival explanations rendered identically when their evidence differs fails §3.10." CLAUDE.md standing constraints, no false equivalence: "A contested claim and an established one do not get parallel presentation."
what_disagrees: Whether rival explanations are rendered at equal visual weight. §4.5 requires equal weight for a bridge's alternatives; V-8 forbids equal weight wherever the evidence is unequal. Both cite §3.10 as their authority.
measured: Not a measurement. Both passages read in full in 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/museum-framework.md as committed on main: §4.5 display rules, and §12.3 constraint V-8.
severity: MEDIUM - it does not affect any evidentiary claim, but it governs how rival explanations are displayed, which is where false equivalence enters a product
resolvable_here: PARTLY. The two rules can be reconciled by scope, and experience-object-model.md §9.7 does so for the Challenge object: reachability is equal for every rival, weight follows evidence. Whether that reconciliation is what museum-framework.md §4.5 intended is the framework author's to say.
effect: experience-object-model.md §9.7 (Challenge rivals) is written against V-8 and CLAUDE.md rather than against §4.5 generalised, and says so at the point of use. An earlier draft of §9.7 asserted that the two rules were not in conflict and cited only §4.5; that was a preferred-counter-narrative failure and is logged as BF-022.
action: Referred to the museum framework for a scope note on §4.5 saying whether it is confined to a bridge and its alternatives. No register row is promoted or demoted by this. Queued in 04-AUDITS/REAUDIT-QUEUE.csv as RA-021.
